newsitem.title: INDIA: Hoechst allowed to up stake in Indian unit.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst allowed to up stake in Indian unit.

text.p: The Indian government has granted permission to German chemicals group Hoechst AG to raise its stake in Hoechst Marion Roussel Ltd, a local subsidiary, a company official said on Friday.
Hoechst AG, which now owns just over 50 percent of Hoechst Marion Roussel, plans to raise its stake to about 55 percent.

Bernhard E. Hofmann, managing director of Hoechst South Asia Investment Ltd, a wholly-owned Hoechst AG subsidiary, said the purchase of shares now held by an institutional investor would raise the parent firm's holding to about 55 percent.
"Government approval has come. SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India, the market regulator) approval is awaited," Hofmann told reporters.

He said United Breweries, Hoechst AG's Indian partner in Hoechst Marion Roussel Ltd, had sold part of its holding to an investment bank which Hoechst AG now plans to acquire. He did not name the investment bank.
United Breweries now owns about 20 percent and the Indian public owns about 25 percent, Hofmann said.
"The shareholding with the Indian public will not be affected," a Hoechst Marion Roussel official said.
